html:
The St'at'imc, or Lillooet, are an Interior Salish people of British Columbia, on the Fraser and Lillooet rivers in the Coast Mountains. Their language, St'at'imcets, is a Salishan language.

Their country sits where the Fraser River runs through a dry, windy canyon. For thousands of years they caught salmon there and dried it in the wind on racks, a food they traded widely. Big villages of pit houses stood along the river. Their neighbours were the Nlaka'pamux downriver and the Secwépemc to the east.

In 1858 the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush brought thousands of miners through their land, followed by roads, settlers and smallpox. In 1911 their chiefs signed the Declaration of the Lillooet Tribe, asserting that they had never given up their land. They remain eleven communities in Canada.
